evidence.note: Consistent measure-after-edit cadence: kernel edits are followed by cycle measurements, showing the agent continuously tracks the current number against changes rather than editing blind.

A persistent memory file (vliw-kernel-structure.md) updated seven times across early/middle/late phases — evidence of a maintained written ledger of structure and progress across a very long trajectory.

Backup named kernel_1468_backup.py shows the agent knew its exact standing (1468 vs 1250 target) and preserved a known-good checkpoint before risking further changes, then discarded it once superseded.

Shift from hand-editing to floor/ideal cost modeling and systematic search scripts (floors, ideal, loadbound, rethink, bigsearch, exhaustive, final_exh) indicates recognizing plateau in manual tuning and redirecting effort — though the volume of late search scripts hints at some circling.

reasoning: The action structure shows the agent reliably re-measures cycles after each change, maintains a repeatedly-updated memory ledger spanning the whole arc, tracks its exact distance to the 1250 target (the 1468-tagged backup), and redirects from hand-tuning to systematic search when progress stalls — behavior matching the level-5 tracking anchor and reaching toward the level-8 'ledger + plateau recognition + redirect' anchor. It falls short of a confident 8 because I cannot verify an explicit transform→cycle-delta ledger or clear stall-flagging from the log alone, and the heavy late-stage search activity leaves some ambiguity about churn, so I place the observed level at 7.
